observations.text: The process starts when a customer sends us a quotation request. From there, I record the request, check the customer’s information in our CRM, and then create the quotation in our quoting system using the customer and pricing information. The intended outcome is to produce an accurate quotation that we can send to the customer by email.

When I check the customer’s information in the CRM, I’m mainly looking at their contact details and any relevant account or pricing information we have on file. That way, I can make sure the quotation is addressed correctly and uses the right pricing for that customer.

When I create the quotation in the quoting system, I basically enter the customer details and the pricing information that we have on file. That’s the main part of it. I don’t think there are any special conditions or branches at that point—it’s pretty straightforward.

When I record the request, I just log the basic details of the quotation request we received from the customer—like who it’s from and what they’re asking for. I keep that in our system so we have a record of it before I move on to checking the customer info and creating the quotation.
Normally, once the quotation is created, I just send it to the customer by email. There aren’t any special checks or conditions before sending it in the usual case.
